Examples include gestational alloimmune liver disease (GALD), tyrosinemia, familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), and some cases of congenital viral (herpes simplex virus [HSV]) infection.

qs.q: A 4-year-old child presents with unremitting high fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and cytopenias. Laboratory evaluation reveals profound hyperferritinemia. Which serum ferritin level is considered highly specific for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis?
qs.e: Extremely high serum ferritin levels greater than 10,000 µg/L are highly specific for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in the appropriate clinical context. Levels between 500 and 1000 µg/L can be seen in various inflammatory states.

qs.q: A critically ill teenager is diagnosed with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis triggered by a viral infection. What constitutes the standard initial medical therapy for this condition?
qs.e: Dexamethasone combined with etoposide forms the backbone of the standard HLH-94/2004 induction treatment protocol. Prednisone and rituximab are primarily used for autoimmune conditions or B-cell malignancies.
qs.s: MDS, Myelofibrosis & HLH: Key Blood Disorders Explained: MCQs

qs.q: A 32-year-old immunosuppressed patient develops multi-organ failure and fever of unknown origin, leading to a diagnosis of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Which pathogen is the most frequent infectious trigger?
qs.e: Epstein-Barr virus is the single most common infectious trigger for secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Cytomegalovirus is also a known trigger, but less common than Epstein-Barr virus.
